title: Escrowed Batch Reveal: Eliminating First-Proposal Bias in Agentic Marketplaces Through Visibility Protocol Design

contributions.purpose: Characterize and quantify first-proposal bias in LLM-mediated marketplaces.
contributions.mechanism: Define first-arrival selection rate and measure how often a customer agent selects the earliest-arriving proposal under standard sequential-visibility protocols (HardGate) in the Magentic Marketplace.
contributions.evaluation: Customer agents (gemini-2.5-flash) select the earliest-arriving proposal 73.3% of the time, more than double the uniform expectation of 33.3% (K=3).
contributions.source_quote: We quantify first-proposal bias in LLM-mediated marketplaces, demonstrating that customer agents select the earliest-arriving proposal 73.3% of the time under standard protocols--more than double the uniform expectation of 33.3%.

contributions.purpose: Eliminate arrival-order bias through a protocol-level change rather than prompting.
contributions.mechanism: Escrowed Batch Reveal (EBR): buffer incoming proposals in a hidden escrow queue, release all K simultaneously once the threshold is reached, and shuffle their order before release, decoupling arrival order from presentation order while holding payment constraints constant.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a three-mechanism protocol (escrow, batch release, shuffle) built on the HardGate payment-gating baseline in Magentic Marketplace.
contributions.source_quote: We propose EBR, a visibility protocol that decouples proposal arrival order from presentation order through escrowed buffering and randomized batch release.

contributions.purpose: Show EBR removes arrival-order bias and that prompt-based interventions do not.
contributions.mechanism: Compare EBR against SoftWait (prompt-only), Inference-Time Scaling, and HardGate on gemini-2.5-flash, with per-scenario, reveal-position, and cross-model analyses.
contributions.evaluation: EBR reduces first-arrival selection from 73.3% to 24.4% (z=4.639, p<0.001, distribution indistinguishable from uniform, chi-squared p=0.494); prompt-based SoftWait/ITS only reach 63.3%.
contributions.domain: Debiasing evaluation for LLM marketplace agents
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that EBR reduces first-arrival selection from 73.3% to 24.4% (p < 0.001), achieving statistical uniformity across arrival positions, while prompt-based interventions achieve only modest reductions to 63.3%.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Bansal et al. (2025) develop Magentic Marketplace, a simulated two-sided marketplace ... revealing that all models exhibit severe first-proposal bias creating 10-30x advantages for response speed over quality.
We evaluate EBR using the Magentic Marketplace (Bansal et al., 2025), an open-source two-sided agentic marketplace environment.

While prior work has documented that LLMs exhibit order effects and that agentic marketplaces suffer from first-proposal bias, we are the first to propose and evaluate a protocol-level intervention--Escrowed Batch Reveal--that eliminates arrival-order bias through visibility control rather than prompt engineering or computational scaling.

notes: Reports a partial negative / limitation: EBR removes arrival-order bias but presentation-order primacy persists (first-revealed proposal still selected 72.7% of the time), so per-transaction bias remains and only statistical fairness is achieved. Cross-model: on claude-sonnet-4-5 the baseline is already near uniform (36.7%), so EBR gives only a non-significant 13.3pp reduction (p=0.13, floor effect); bias is model-dependent.
